name: Mount Fuji by the Yoshida trail (富士山 吉田ルート)
why: Japan's highest mountain on its most-walked trail: climb to a hut at 3,000 m, sleep a few hours and reach the crater rim for sunrise over the clouds.
book: Open only in the official season, about 1 July to 10 September. Register online and pay the 4,000 yen climbing fee; no entry from 14:00 to 03:00 unless you have a hut booking. Book the hut months ahead: tents are not allowed. Buses to the 5th station from Kawaguchiko and Fujisan stations.
water: No water on the mountain: buy it at the 5th station or at the huts (expensive higher up). Carry 2 litres.
dangers: Altitude: headaches and nausea above 3,000 m. Go slowly, sleep at the hut and go down if it gets worse.
Near 0°C before sunrise at the top, with wind: down jacket, gloves and hat even in August.
Falling rocks and crowds near the summit: do not overtake on the edge, a helmet is recommended.
Thunderstorms in the afternoon: there is no shelter on the bare slope above the huts.
turnaround: If you have a strong headache or vomit, go down at once: the only cure is lower altitude.

points.name: Fuji Subaru Line 5th Station
points.note: 2,305 m, at the end of the bus road: shops, toilets and the information centre. Spend an hour here to get used to the altitude.

points.name: 8th Station huts
points.note: A string of huts from the 7th to the Original 8th station, about 2,700-3,400 m. Dinner, a few hours on a futon, and off again around 01:00-02:00 for sunrise.

points.name: Fuji crater rim, top of the Yoshida trail
points.note: About 3,710 m at Kusushi shrine on the rim; the true summit, 3,776 m, is on the far side of the crater. Go down by the separate descent trail: follow the yellow signs at the 8th station.
